Observed-data log-likelihood of the longitudinal sub-model

Source: R/fitImputedBJM.R
observedLongLogLik.Rd

Experimental. Compares longitudinal sub-models fitted to the same right-censored data, e.g. different forms of the event-time effect in long_sub_fixed, or a fit on the subjects with an event against fitImputedBJM. A subject with an event contributes \(\log f(Y \mid T, D)\) at the observed \(T\) (and event type); a censored subject contributes \(\log \int_C^\infty \sum_d f(Y \mid t, d) P(d \mid t) \, dF(t) - \log S(C)\), so the censored subjects count too. The factors \(f(T)\) and \(P(D \mid T)\) of the events do not involve the longitudinal sub-model and are left out, so only differences between fits sharing survival_fit_all are meaningful. Higher is better; the fits compared should have the same number of parameters, or the difference be judged with that in mind.

Usage

observedLongLogLik(
  fit,
  data_survival,
  data_fit_all,
  time_variable,
  survival_variable_all = NULL,
  survival_trans_function = NULL,
  n_grid = 40
)

Arguments

fit

A "fitImputedBJM" object (its log-likelihood is averaged over the imputations' fits), or a list with long_fit_all and survival_fit_all.

data_survival, data_fit_all

The data the fit was made on, as in fitImputedBJM: every subject, with the observed event or censoring time.

time_variable, survival_variable_all, survival_trans_function

As in predictRisk.

n_grid

Grid points per censored subject.

Value

The log-likelihood (a number).
